candidates.title: About 105,000 transients on the pre-Sputnik Palomar plates
candidates.quote: Our original sample is around uh, 105,000 transients from just the northern hemisphere,

link.reason: Both tell of the roughly 100,000 transients Villarroel found on the pre-Sputnik Palomar plates.
link.difference: Told first hand by Villarroel, who gives about 105,000 and says the sample covers only the northern hemisphere.

candidates.title: Five transients appearing and vanishing on 27 July 1952
candidates.quote: One is five objects on a narrow band. And it's from the 27th of July 1952.

link.reason: The story on July 1952 plates covers both the 19 and 27 July cases together. This telling is only the 27 July case, so it is narrower.

candidates.title: Three bright transients on 19 July 1952 found by Enrique Solano
candidates.quote: And then my colleague Enrique Solano in Spain, he discovered another such really beautiful example with three super bright beautiful stars. It's the most beautiful example of all we have. This one is from the 19th of July, 1952.

link.reason: Only the 19 July 1952 triple transient found by Solano, one case inside the combined July 1952 story. It is also a different case from #2.

candidates.title: Dave Altman connects the transient dates to the Washington flap
candidates.quote: And then my colleague, Dave Altman, who is the manager media manager for WASCO, he said, "Do you know what happens on or what happened on 19th of July, 1952?"

link.reason: Altman linking the transient dates to the Washington flap is a separate testimony. It is not the DC sightings themselves, and it is not the plate transients.

candidates.title: 1952 Washington UFO flap
candidates.quote: It prompted a call between Truman and Edward J. Ruppelt, who was the head of Blue Book at the time.

link.reason: The July 1952 Washington UFO flap and the call between Truman and Ruppelt.
link.difference: Calls Ruppelt the head of Blue Book at the time.

candidates.title: Earth's shadow test shows a deficit of transients
candidates.place_text: Palomar plates; about 42,164 km from Earth (geosynchronous distance)
candidates.quote: And guess what? We get a huge deficit.

link.reason: Both tell of the Palomar transients being missing inside Earth's shadow.
link.difference: Told first hand by Villarroel. She calls it a huge deficit, places it at geosynchronous distance and credits Guy Nir.

candidates.title: Donald Menzel destroys a third of the Harvard plates
candidates.quote: And two or three months after, he suddenly becomes the director of Harvard Observatory, and he destroys 1/3 of the photographic plates.

link.reason: Menzel destroying Harvard plates, as documented by Dorrit Hoffleit.
link.difference: Says it was a third of the plates, done in 1952 soon after Menzel became director.

candidates.title: Presidential advisor held UFO material from a 1963 Marshall Islands nuclear detonation
candidates.quote: We've even interviewed a top presidential advisor at the end of his life who admitted to holding UFO material that came from a nuclear detonation in the Marshall Islands in late 1963.

link.reason: A presidential advisor holding UFO material from a late-1963 Marshall Islands detonation. The Johnston Island story is about recovering an object after a Soviet orbital nuke was shot down, and the Malmgren story is about telepathy. Neither makes this core claim.

candidates.title: Robert Hastings' 167 Q-cleared witnesses of UFOs at nuclear sites
candidates.quote: Robert Hastings, author of the book UFOs and Nukes, who's chronicled 167 Q-cleared nuclear base employees who have blown the whistle on UFOs showing up all over our nuclear installations.

link.reason: Hastings' book UFOs and Nukes and its 167 witnesses from nuclear bases.

candidates.title: Roswell held the most US nukes in 1947
candidates.quote: Roswell was the site of the most nukes in the US in 1947 at the time of the Roswell crash.

link.reason: A claim about how many nuclear weapons were at Roswell in 1947. The Roswell crash story is about the crash and only mentions the base in passing.

candidates.title: UFOs at Mount Sengan Mori, Iino, next to Fukushima
candidates.quote: go as far as Japan, where a town named Iino, which is right next to the Fukushima prefecture, has a mountain, Mount Sengan Mori, where UFOs constantly show up.

link.reason: Both tell of UFOs around the town of Iino/Eno, next to the Fukushima prefecture.
link.difference: Names Mount Sengan Mori as the place where the UFOs keep appearing and leaves out the Vice article and the 2011 disaster.

candidates.title: Ariel School landing in Zimbabwe, near a uranium mine
candidates.quote: In the '90s in Zimbabwe, over 60 schoolchildren all saw a UFO land and an alien descend out of the craft and telepathically speak to them.

link.reason: Both tell of the Ariel School landing in Zimbabwe, near a uranium mine, seen by schoolchildren.
link.difference: Says over 60 children saw it in the '90s and adds that a being came out and spoke to them telepathically.

candidates.title: Classified lists of uncorrelated targets since the 1960s
candidates.place_text: Earth orbit; US Space Force, NASA, ESA
candidates.quote: What I didn't know is that there's apparently since the early 1960s, there were something called uncorrelated targets.

link.reason: Both are about NASA and the Space Force tracking 'uncorrelated targets' in orbit, and both trace back to Villarroel.

downgraded.why: a program telling and the testimony story nasa-space-force-track-uncorrelated-targets-2020: a program and a story of another kind are different grains

candidates.title: Keyhoe: Air Force tracked two unknown satellites in 1953
candidates.quote: Keyhoe states something astonishing, that the Air Force was tracking two unknown artificial satellites 400 and 600 miles up in low Earth orbit.

link.reason: Keyhoe's claim that the Air Force tracked two unknown satellites in 1953 matches no story below; the uncorrelated-targets story is a different, broader claim.

candidates.title: White Sands near-Earth satellite search led by LaPaz and Tombaugh
candidates.place_text: White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico
candidates.quote: That same year, a very unusual project started at White Sands Missile Range.
documents: Near Earth Satellite Project final report

link.reason: No story covers the 1953-54 near-Earth satellite search at White Sands led by LaPaz and Tombaugh. The LaPaz green-fireball stories are a different program.

candidates.title: Project Twinkle green fireballs
candidates.place_text: Los Alamos; Holloman Air Force Base
candidates.quote: LaPaz headed up Project Twinkle, an Air Force investigation into unexplained green fireballs showing up across American nuclear sites,

link.reason: Both describe Project Twinkle, the Air Force investigation of green fireballs headed by LaPaz.
link.difference: Places the fireballs at nuclear sites across the US, naming Los Alamos and Holloman AFB.

candidates.title: LaPaz statement in Aviation Week on two unknown objects
candidates.quote: On August 23rd, 1954, Aviation Week and Space Technology published a statement from LaPaz,
documents: Aviation Week and Space Technology, August 23, 1954
Near Earth Satellite Project final report

link.reason: LaPaz's statement in Aviation Week on 23 August 1954 is one specific document inside the satellite search. No story covers it.

candidates.title: Government documents describe metallic, reflective, flat-bottomed objects
candidates.quote: These documents include the 1947 Twining memo, the 1948 Project Sign analysis, and the CIA's analysis of the 1952 DC UFO flyover, along with Blue Book lead Captain Edward J. Ruppelt's analysis and more.
documents: CIA analysis of the 1952 DC UFO flyover

link.reason: This groups several documents (Twining memo, Project Sign, CIA analysis of the 1952 DC flyover, Ruppelt) under one claim that the objects were metallic and reflective. That is broader than the Twining memo story.

candidates.title: Steven Bruel's study links transients to nuclear tests and UAP reports
candidates.quote: And he finds a correlation. It's weak, but it's there and it's statistically significant.

link.reason: Both describe the same study linking Palomar transients to nuclear tests, which the story's teller already credits to Bruehl and Villarroel.
link.difference: Credits Bruel as the author, calls the correlation weak but statistically significant, and adds a link to UAP reports.

candidates.title: 68% rise in transients the day after a nuclear test
candidates.place_text: Palomar Observatory; Nevada, New Mexico, Pacific, Kazakhstan, Australia test sites
candidates.quote: But if there's been a a nuclear test the day before, then it's uh almost 19% of those days have a transient.
documents: Center for UFO Studies UFOCAT database

link.reason: Both state the same finding: transients are 68% more likely the day after a nuclear test.
link.difference: Told by Bruel himself, with the rate of about 19% of days, the named test sites and the UFOCAT database.

candidates.title: No transient-nuclear test matches after 17 March 1956
candidates.quote: uh the last time we saw a correspondence between a nuclear test and a uh transient was March 17th, 1956.

link.reason: This telling is about the last match between a nuclear test and a transient, on 17 March 1956. The Villarroel story makes the general claim that transients correlate with nuclear tests, so a cutoff date inside that correlation is a narrower claim.

candidates.title: Larry Hancock: UAP at nuclear facilities 1949-1953, then stopped
candidates.quote: And what they found was high levels of activity from 1949 until 1953, and then it just stopped.

link.reason: This is Larry Hancock's finding that UAP activity at nuclear facilities ran from 1949 to 1953 and then stopped. The nearest stories (Karl Nell on UAP at nuclear sites, Ruppelt's cases near nuclear facilities) are different sources making different claims.

candidates.title: Harry Turner, UFO-obsessed intelligence chief over Woomera nuclear tests
candidates.quote: There's Woomera test range which um the head of the nuclear division actually in Australia, the joint intelligence organization was a guy named Harry Turner, and he was obsessed with UFOs.

link.reason: This telling is about Harry Turner himself: his role as intelligence chief over the Woomera nuclear tests and his obsession with UFOs. The Turner stories in the corpus are about one document (the 1971 report) or one investigation (the Maralinga sightings), which are narrower than a portrait of the man.

candidates.title: NICAP's founding as a possible link to the 1956 cutoff
candidates.quote: that's when NICAP formed, which was the first civilian UFO research program.

link.reason: This is a theory linking NICAP's founding to the 1956 cutoff in transients. The stories about Brown founding NICAP tell the founding as a program, not as an explanation for the cutoff.

candidates.title: International Geophysical Year and the Antarctic no-fly zone
candidates.quote: That's when the International Geophysical Year happened, where Antarctica became a no-fly zone, and a

link.reason: No story in the corpus is about the International Geophysical Year making Antarctica a no-fly zone.

candidates.title: Frank Drake's Project Ozma
candidates.quote: >> In 1961, legendary astronomer Frank Drake started project Ozma, the first ever organized search for interstellar radio signals.

link.reason: No story in the corpus is about Frank Drake's Project Ozma.

candidates.title: The Wow signal
candidates.quote: like the famous Wow signal discovered by Gerry Eman at Ohio State,

link.reason: No story in the corpus is about the 1977 Wow signal at Ohio State.

candidates.title: Bracewell probe possibly lurking in the solar system
candidates.quote: Bracewell took his speculation one step further by considering that such a probe may already be lurking somewhere in the dark recesses of our solar system,

link.reason: No story in the corpus is about a Bracewell probe lurking in the solar system.

candidates.title: Long delay radio echoes heard by Norwegian operators
candidates.quote: The story begins back in 1927. Norwegian shortwave radio operators began to notice something odd.

link.reason: This telling is the 1927 event itself: Norwegian radio operators first hearing long delay echoes. The existing long delay echo stories are theories about the echoes (that they inspired Sagan's Contact, or that Kordylewski clouds cause them), not the first observation.

candidates.title: Long delay echoes rise when Earth-Moon L5 is above the horizon
candidates.quote: And one study even found a statistically significant increase in LDEs when the Earth-Moon L5 Lagrange point was above the horizon.

link.reason: This telling cites a statistical study finding more long delay echoes when the Earth-Moon L5 point is above the horizon. The Kordylewski story credits Robert Temple with explaining the echoes as plasma clouds, which is a different claim from a measured correlation.

candidates.title: Villarroel approached by people she suspects have intelligence backgrounds
candidates.quote: I have been approached by some people I suspect have it.

link.reason: Villarroel's own account of being approached by people she suspects have intelligence ties. No story below covers this.

candidates.title: Vera Rubin telescope to remove classified satellites from its data
candidates.quote: fact that the Vera Rubin telescope is going to remove a lot of classified satellites and other objects.

link.reason: A claim that the Vera Rubin Observatory will remove classified satellites from its data. Immaculate Constellation is a different program about sequestering data.

candidates.title: Jacques Vallee's retrograde orbiting object at the Paris Observatory
candidates.quote: One night on July 11th, 1961, he and his colleagues noticed something truly bizarre. An unidentified object orbiting the Earth.

link.reason: Vallee's 1961 sighting of an unknown orbiting object at the Paris Observatory. Vallee's sighting at age 15 is a different event.

candidates.title: Vallee's orbital mystery object seen by multiple observatories and US tracking stations
candidates.quote: Vallee pointed out in a later interview, "Later, I found out that other observatories had made exactly the same observation, and that in fact American tracking stations had photographed the same thing and couldn't identify it either. It was as bright as the star Sirius. You couldn't miss it. It didn't reappear in successive weeks.

link.reason: The same mystery orbiting object Vallee saw in telling 3, now with corroboration from other observatories and US tracking stations.
link.difference: Adds that other observatories and US tracking stations recorded the object, that it was as bright as Sirius, and that it did not reappear.

candidates.title: Corona spy satellite program offered as explanation for Vallee's sighting
candidates.quote: sighting by invoking the Corona program, a series of highly secretive CIA-sponsored satellites first launched in 1960, kicking off the modern era of orbital espionage. The Corona satellites did have a nearly polar orbit. However, it's a very insufficient explanation.

link.reason: Offers the CIA Corona spy satellites as the explanation for the same orbiting object in telling 3, which is a different core claim about what the light was.
link.difference: Explains the object as a polar-orbit Corona satellite launched from 1960 on, though the host calls this explanation insufficient.

candidates.title: Paul Muller confiscates and destroys Vallee's tracking tape
candidates.quote: His superior at the observatory, Paul Muller, got a hold of the data. The next morning, Muller, who behaved like a petty army officer, simply confiscated the tape and destroyed it.

link.reason: Muller seizing and destroying the tracking tape is a single incident inside the larger sighting story, so it is narrower than telling 3.

candidates.title: Chief of aerospace medicine attached to NASA and the Air Force saw something
candidates.quote: I just interviewed a uh uh chief uh of aerospace medicine, you know, one of the top doctors. He was attached to NASA. He was at the the Air Force. He was a senior doctor there. Uh and he saw something.

link.reason: A senior aerospace medicine doctor attached to NASA and the Air Force who saw something. No story below matches this witness.

candidates.title: Tens of thousands of alien satellites studying Earth before Sputnik
candidates.quote: that tens of thousands of alien satellites were studying our planet before we could even launch one of our own.

link.reason: A general theory that tens of thousands of alien satellites studied Earth before Sputnik. The Palomar transients story is the specific plate finding, not this broader theory.
